item: Basement encapsulation system (skip-list — usually overkill)
paybackNotes: Skip before knowing the moisture source; often replaces a ~$300 downspout+grading fix. Interior French drain systems $5,000-12,000 also flagged as skip before exterior fixes. Whole-house dehumidifiers $2,500-4,500 installed flagged as skip when a $300 portable handles 90% of VT basements.

item: Basement finishing, 800-1,200 sq ft typical project
paybackNotes: Only works if basement stays dry — 60% humidity is the mold-growth threshold (EPA / VT DoH). Cost-reality guide: $30-80/sq ft, 600 sq ft = $18,000-48,000.

item: Basement moisture-prep diagnostic kit (hygrometer, moisture meter, water alarms, dehumidifier, mold test)
paybackNotes: Run 30+ days including a wet stretch. Components: WiFi hygrometer $30-80; moisture meter $40-80; water alarms $15-50 battery / $40-80 WiFi; mold screening kit $20-50. Humidity-fix kit (dehumidifier + rim joist sealing) $250-600.

item: Certified mold inspection
paybackNotes: Visible mold over ~10 sq ft is professional remediation territory per EPA guidance.

item: Cheap basement diagnostic (hygrometer + wood moisture meter)
paybackNotes: Hygrometer $15-20 + wood moisture meter $15-25. Thresholds: over 60% sustained humidity = active moisture problem; over 18% wood moisture = rot risk. 'Prevents the most common $30,000 mistake in Vermont home renovation.'

item: Dehumidifier, 50-pint, continuous drain (permanent infrastructure for finished VT basement)
paybackNotes: Operating cost ~$15-25/month in summer, less in winter. Basement-buy-skip-wait guide prices a 50-70 pint unit at $200-450; fall (October) model-year sales bring 25-40% discounts.

item: Egress window install (required for basement bedroom use)
paybackNotes: Basement bathroom rough-in addition: $5,000-12,000. Moisture mitigation before finishing: $1,500-8,000.

item: Foundation drainage repair (interior/exterior perimeter drain, sump pump, crack repair)
paybackNotes: Required when basement takes active water during storms or snowmelt; not a DIY-kit problem.

item: Surface-water fixes: downspout extensions + regrading
paybackNotes: Downspout extensions $10-25 each (discharge 6+ feet from foundation); perimeter grading fix often a $200 weekend with a shovel (slope away 6 inches in first 10 feet). Guide: half of wet-basement problems are surface water. Crawlspace 6-mil poly vapor barrier: $1-2/sq ft.

item: Composite deck, installed
paybackNotes: Mid-size composite with aluminum railing and stairs: $18,000-28,000; premium with hidden fasteners/lighting/multi-level: $35,000-40,000. Railing adds $80-150 per linear foot; hidden fastener systems add $1,000-2,500. Composite carries 25-30 year warranties. Cost-reality guide: composite $60-85/sq ft, cedar $50-65/sq ft.

item: Deck build per square foot (200 sq ft deck = $6,000-16,000)
paybackNotes: $30-80/sq ft. Drivers: material, height over 30 inches (requires more structure/engineering review), freestanding vs attached. Footings must go below frost depth (typically 48-60 inches in VT).

item: Pressure-treated wood deck, installed
paybackNotes: Basic 10x16 with simple stairs: $8,000-12,000. PT decks last 15-25 years with maintenance. Cost-reality guide: PT at $30-40/sq ft.

item: Attic cellulose blow-in to R-49 (from typical R-19/R-30)
paybackNotes: Vermont attic R-value target R-49 to R-60.

item: Comprehensive retrofit rebate stack, income-eligible tier (full retrofit, GMP territory)

rebate.program: EVT ducted + fuel-switching + electrical + weatherization 90% + GMP $2,000/condenser + EVT heat pump water heater
rebate.amount: $11,100-14,700 total stack

paybackNotes: Out-of-pocket: $5,300-13,900. Standard vs income-eligible tiers are mutually exclusive.

item: Comprehensive retrofit rebate stack, standard tier (heat pump + weatherization + electrical, GMP territory)

rebate.program: EVT ducted + EVT fuel-switching + EVT electrical service upgrade + EVT weatherization 75%
rebate.amount: $6,600-8,600 total stack

paybackNotes: Out-of-pocket on $20,000-22,000 combined project: $11,400-15,400. Verified April 2026 per guide.

item: DIY storm window insert kit (magnetic/friction-fit acrylic), per window
paybackNotes: Same-day at hardware stores. Lifespan 3-5 years; magnetic strips can fail. Typically no EVT rebate (not a qualifying product class). Thermal R-value improvement similar across WindowDressers/Indow/DIY.

item: DIY weatherization materials (caulk, weatherstripping, foam sealant, attic hatch kits)

rebate.amount: $100 cash back on materials; submit receipts within 90 days of purchase

paybackNotes: Only rebate in the program not paid through a contractor.

item: EVT energy audit (blower-door test)

rebate.amount: Often free for income-eligible households

paybackNotes: Produces scope of work and rebate-eligibility map; informs heat pump sizing.

item: Historic wood-sash window restoration with custom storm inserts, per window
paybackNotes: vs. $1,200-1,800 for like-for-like custom replacement. Right choice for pre-1900 homes.

item: Indow custom acrylic window insert, per window installed

rebate.amount: Limited EVT rebate support, varies by program year

paybackNotes: 4-8 week lead time. Lifespan 10-15 years; replacement silicone edges available. 8-window farmhouse: $2,400-4,000.

item: Pre-replacement weatherization spend (diagnostic-first, per-house)
paybackNotes: Cost-reality guide window section: 'Pre-weatherization spend before deciding: $200-485 typical.' If after one season of ~$200 in fixes windows are still cold, replacement is the right call.

item: Wall insulation upgrade, typical 2,000 sq ft home (dense-pack cellulose)
paybackNotes: Longer payback than attic/rim-joist scope per guide.

item: Weatherization payback period (typical scope, energy savings alone)
paybackNotes: 3-7 years on energy savings alone for typical scopes — faster than nearly any other US state due to 7,500-8,500 annual heating degree days. Weatherizing before heat pump makes sizing math 15-25% cheaper.

item: Whole-home weatherization (air sealing + insulation), project scope

rebate.program: EVT Home Performance with ENERGY STAR — standard tier
rebate.amount: 75% of project cost; total out-of-pocket after rebate runs $1,000-4,500 standard tier

paybackNotes: From facts.ts single-source-of-truth ('vt-cost-weatherization-whole-home', verified 2026-04-15), referenced by weatherization and rebate-stack guides via factIds.

item: Whole-project weatherization, EVT income-eligible tier (90% of project cost)

rebate.amount: 90% of project cost; stacked rebates cap around $16,700; qualifying threshold 80% AMI

paybackNotes: Example: $6,000 scope → $600 out-of-pocket. $18,000 deep retrofit → rebate ~$16,700 capped, out-of-pocket $1,300.

item: Whole-project weatherization, EVT standard tier (75% of project cost)

rebate.program: EVT Home Performance with ENERGY STAR — standard tier
rebate.amount: 75% of project cost; stacked rebates cap around $7,700

paybackNotes: Example: $6,000 scope → $4,500 paid by EVT to contractor, $1,500 out-of-pocket. $12,000 full scope hits ~$7,700 cap, out-of-pocket $4,300. Rebate paid to contractor, not homeowner.

item: Window draft-fix core cart (V-strip, film, caulk, door sweep)
paybackNotes: Optional add-ons push to $255-485. Components: weatherstripping $15-35/pack (V-strip/silicone lasts 5-10 years; foam crushes in 3 months); shrink film $15/kit covers 3-5 windows; caulk $10-20; door-bottom sweep $8-25; storm insert kit ~$30-50/window. Handles a typical VT farmhouse for 1-2 winters.

item: Window weatherization kit (film + weatherstripping + sash caulk + draft control)
paybackNotes: Closes 70-90% of air leakage on a leaky pre-1990 window; buys 5-10 more years on many windows. Air-leak fixes pay back in one winter on most pre-1990 homes (7,500-8,500 HDD). Per-window materials: $20-60 air-leak fix; film $15-80; interior storm inserts $200-400.

item: Window weatherization seasonal savings

rebate.program: Efficiency Vermont / Community Action Partnership (CAP) agencies
rebate.amount: EVT incentives for ENERGY STAR-qualified window replacement; income-eligible weatherization assistance via CAP; guide claims stacking with federal IRA 25C credits

paybackNotes: Guide: drafty windows can account for 10-25% of a VT heating bill (attributed to EVT); honest weatherization commonly cuts draft loss 50-70% for a season = $200-800 saved per winter. STALE-DATE CAVEAT: the 25C stacking claim conflicts with topic guides stating 25C expired Dec 31, 2025. Timing: window kits drop 30-40% in March-April clearance.

item: WindowDressers community-built interior storm window insert, per insert

rebate.amount: EVT rebate support — qualifying installations get incentive (amount not stated)

paybackNotes: ~$40 per insert at the community build. 4-6 month lead time (sign up summer for November build). Lasts 10+ years with seasonal removal and flat storage.

item: Cold-climate heat pump (Efficiency Vermont rebate, per heat pump)

rebate.amount: $800 to $2,000 per cold-climate heat pump

paybackNotes: Must use a participating contractor; application within 90 days. Applies to both primary and secondary homes. NOTE: conflicts with newer topic guides that state a flat $2,200 ducted / $475-per-head ductless structure — this guide's figure appears to be older program framing.

item: Ducted cold-climate heat pump, single whole-house system, installed

rebate.amount: $2,200 per system, paid by EVT to participating contractor at job completion

paybackNotes: Statewide median; resort-tier towns reach $14,000-28,000. Verified April 2026 per guide.

item: Ductless heat pump indoor head (EVT rebate, per head)

rebate.amount: $475 per indoor head; a 3-head system = $1,425

paybackNotes: Multiple heads stack within program rules.

item: Ductwork retrofit in old home (heat pump cost driver)
paybackNotes: Other drivers: tight installs requiring custom refrigerant line routing $1,000-3,000.

item: Electrical service/panel upgrade tied to electrification

rebate.amount: $500; requires a paired heat pump or EV charger install

paybackNotes: Cost range is the 'old wiring requiring service upgrade' driver cited in the same guide. Standalone panel upgrades don't get the rebate.

item: Federal Section 25C credit on heat pumps (status)
paybackNotes: 2026 stack is EVT + utility-side bonus only. Section 25D (30%, still active) applies to solar PV + battery, not heat pumps. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: GMP income-eligible heat pump bonus (per condenser)

rebate.program: Utility-side bonus (GMP only) — Green Mountain Power
rebate.amount: $2,000 per condenser for income-eligible customers (household at or below 80% AMI)

paybackNotes: Chittenden County 3-person 80% AMI around $96,750 (2026); most rural counties run 15-25% lower.

item: Heat pump installation, all configurations, before rebates
paybackNotes: Single-zone ductless $3,000-6,000; multi-zone whole-home (3-5 zones) $12,000-30,000; ducted central $8,000-18,000. STALE-DATE CAVEAT: 25C claim conflicts with rebate-stack topic guides (25C expired Dec 31, 2025); EVT amount also disagrees with the flat $2,200/$475 structure in the 2026 topic guides. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: Heat pump water heater, installed

rebate.amount: $600; stacks with heat pump install; self-install allowed with electrician permit

paybackNotes: Net after $600 EVT rebate: $1,900-3,900.

item: Multi-zone ductless heat pump (2-3 rooms), installed
Oil-to-electric fuel switch (removing oil furnace/boiler as primary heat)

rebate.amount: $400, on top of the ducted rebate; documentation of fuel switch required

item: Single-zone ductless mini-split, installed
paybackNotes: Guide: 'For most seasonal homes, one or two single-zone units in the main living area and primary bedroom is the sweet spot. After rebates: $2,000 to $4,000.'

item: Standard-tier heat pump stack, GMP territory, oil-to-electric, single ducted

rebate.program: EVT ducted + EVT fuel-switching + EVT electrical service upgrade

paybackNotes: Out-of-pocket: $11,000-13,000. Income-eligible GMP adds $2,000 → total $5,100, out-of-pocket $9,000-11,000.

item: Typical $4,500 mini-split install, stacked incentives example
paybackNotes: STALE-DATE CAVEAT: this guide treats the federal 25C credit (30% up to $2,000/yr) as active; the 2026 topic guides state 25C expired December 31, 2025. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: VPPSA member-utility income-eligible heat pump bonus (per condenser)

rebate.amount: $1,000 per condenser for income-eligible customers

paybackNotes: VPPSA towns: Hyde Park, Stowe, Northfield, Ludlow, Lyndonville, Hardwick, Morrisville, Enosburg, Swanton, Barton, Jacksonville, Johnson, Orleans, Readsboro. BED (Burlington) does NOT stack this way.

item: Cabinet refinishing supplies (vs door replacement)
paybackNotes: New cabinet doors run $80-200 per door installed — $2,000-5,000 for a 25-door kitchen. Refinishing the same set: $150-300 in materials and a weekend, looks 90% as good.

item: Kitchen cosmetic refresh, DIY materials (no cabinets, no structural)
paybackNotes: Contractor version of same scope: $3,000-8,000.

item: Kitchen full gut renovation (custom cabinetry, structural changes)
paybackNotes: $120,000+ open-ended top. 3-5 months demolition to punch list. Older VT homes often add code-update work (knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized plumbing). Cost-reality guide extends full renovation to $60,000-150,000+.

item: Kitchen mid-range renovation (semi-custom cabinets, quartz/granite)
paybackNotes: Most common VT range. 6-10 weeks once materials arrive. Budget a 15-20% contingency on older homes. NOTE: cost-reality guide gives mid-range as $30,000-60,000 and facts.ts as $35,000-65,000 — ranges disagree across guides.

item: Kitchen minor refresh (finishes only, no layout change)
paybackNotes: Cabinet refacing/repainting, laminate or entry-level quartz, new sink/faucet/hardware, lighting, mid-range appliances. Completes in 2-4 weeks.

item: Kitchen refresh core 3 moves (hardware swap + faucet + under-cabinet lighting)
paybackNotes: Cabinet hardware $80-180 full kitchen (20-30 pulls); faucet $140-220 (Moen/Delta mid-range); plug-in LED under-cabinet strips $40-80. Highest-ROI low-spend project per guide.

item: Water alarms for leak-prone basement zones
paybackNotes: $15-50 battery alarms or $40-80 WiFi sensors. Place under water heater, washer, near sump, and at basement low point; run a full season including a rainstorm and a snowmelt.

item: Under-cabinet LED strip lighting, plug-in (no electrical work)
paybackNotes: Timing: LED strip pricing drops 25-40% in November (holiday cycle).

item: Architect fees for typical residential ADU design
paybackNotes: Design-build contractors sometimes bundle design into the contract.

item: Bathroom remodel, full gut (studs, new rough-in, radiant floor, custom tile)
paybackNotes: $55,000+ open-ended. 4-8 weeks active construction; older homes add time for knob-and-tube, galvanized pipe, subfloor damage.

item: Bathroom remodel, mid-range renovation
paybackNotes: 2-4 weeks active construction (new tile, modest fixture relocation, new shower/tub surround).

item: Bathroom remodel, minor refresh
paybackNotes: 1-2 weeks active construction; same-layout scope typically needs no permit. Lead time before demo: 6-10 weeks (contractor booking 3-6 weeks out, tile 4-8 weeks, permits 2-4 weeks).

item: Contractor deposit norms and registration threshold
paybackNotes: Deposit 20-33% on signing is standard; over 33% is a yellow flag. Guide cites 9 V.S.A. § 4205 requiring registered contractors for jobs over $10,000. NOTE: the rebate-stack topic guides instead cite the VT AG Consumer Assistance Program registration threshold at $3,500+ — the two thresholds/statutes conflict across guides.

item: Detached ADU, 700-900 sq ft, fully built
paybackNotes: Resort-tier towns reach $140,000-230,000. Attached ADU: $90,000-180,000. Garage conversion: $50,000-130,000. Total elapsed time 12-18 months; build phase 4-8 months detached. Verified April 2026 per guide.

item: Handyman labor rate (facts.ts canonical, cross-guide reference)
paybackNotes: $40-75/hour or $300-600/day, materials extra; full seasonal prep visit with materials $400-800. From facts.ts 'vt-cost-handyman-rate' (verified 2026-04-15).

item: Lake season outdoor setup (first-time Champlain camp/lake property)
paybackNotes: Lean mid-tier setup $2,400-3,800; catalog-driven $4,800-7,500; premium custom $8,000-15,000+. Memorial Day vs November buying: 30-50% price differential on furniture.

item: Renovation durations (planning claims)
paybackNotes: Kitchen 6-14 weeks; bathroom 3-6 weeks; basement finishing 6-10 weeks; deck 1-3 weeks; roof replacement 1-4 days; whole-house window replacement 1-3 days; heat pump install 2-5 days. Add 4-12 weeks lead time for contractor availability. Winter interior-work discounts: some contractors discount 5-15% for January-March schedules.

item: Septic system upgrade, conventional (ADU capacity trigger)
paybackNotes: Engineered/mound systems: $30,000-45,000. Vermont sizes septic by bedroom count with a 'could be used as' bedroom test.

item: Deck building permit (required in all VT municipalities)
paybackNotes: Cost figure from cost-reality guide ('Permitting in most VT towns: $100-500'). Deck guide: plan 2-4 weeks for approval; structural inspection during framing; no size threshold exempts residential decks.

item: Residential renovation building permit fees (most municipalities)
paybackNotes: Varies by municipality and project size; larger projects often calculated as a percentage of project value. Review takes 2-4 weeks for standard residential work.

item: Short-term rental (STR) town registration for ADU
paybackNotes: Per year, typical. Vermont state lodging tax 9% combined also applies to STRs.

item: Town building permit for ADU
paybackNotes: Processing 2-8 weeks. Resort towns layer on design review costs $1,500-5,000. Total ADU permit burden per guide: $2,000-5,000 in state wastewater permits, septic engineer fees, and town permits.

item: Vermont DEC wastewater/potable water permit (ADU or added bedroom capacity)
paybackNotes: Plus $500-1,500 for licensed septic engineer's evaluation. Processing 4-12 weeks. Triggered by nearly all ADUs.

item: EVT audit-driven scope priority (what to fix before windows)
paybackNotes: EVT audit sequencing puts rim-joist and attic-plate air sealing ahead of window replacement on typical pre-1990 VT homes; window replacement is rarely the highest-payback scope on a VT blower-door report. Trap cited: spending $10,000 on windows when the same money on professional weatherization would save 4x the energy.

item: Asphalt shingle roof replacement
paybackNotes: 1,500 sq ft ranch in Burlington: $9,000-13,000 installed. Standard asphalt lasts 20-25 years in VT; architectural 25-30 years.

item: Roof replacement before solar (standing seam vs asphalt, from solar sequencing section)
paybackNotes: Standing seam metal $14,000-32,000 (40-70 year life); architectural asphalt $8,000-20,000 (25-30 year life). Rebate stack is empty for the roof itself; solar credits apply only to solar work.

item: Roofing per-square pricing (2,000 sq ft roof = 20 squares runs $8,000-24,000)
paybackNotes: Architectural asphalt (30-yr): $400-600/square. Standing-seam metal (60+ yr): $900-1,400/square. Cedar shake: $1,200-2,000/square. Tear-off and disposal: $1,000-3,000 added. NOTE: standing-seam per-square range here ($900-1,400) runs higher than the roof guide's $600-900.

item: Standing seam metal roof
paybackNotes: $600-900 per square (100 sq ft). Metal lasts 40-70 years, sheds snow, resists ice dams. Metal roofing overall: $15,000-40,000; steel panels mid-range $15,000-25,000 at $400-600/square.

item: 8kW solar + 13.5 kWh battery, gross install
paybackNotes: Net after upfront credits example: $50,000 - $15,000 (25D) - $5,400 (EVT) = $29,600. System produces $1,800-2,400/year retail-rate offset plus ~$285/year net-metering adder credits. Guide's net range after credits: $28,000-42,000. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: Battery storage paired with solar (EVT incentive)

rebate.amount: $0.40/Wh of battery capacity — Tesla Powerwall (13.5 kWh) = $5,400; Enphase pair (20 kWh) = $8,000

paybackNotes: Battery must be paired with solar; standalone storage doesn't qualify. Paid through participating contractor at install completion. Incentive can be reduced if homeowner declines grid-services participation.

item: Solar + battery + heat pump combined stack, standard tier (on ~$65,000 combined project)
paybackNotes: Components: 25D $15,000 (on $50,000 solar+battery), EVT solar+storage $5,400 (Powerwall 13.5 kWh), EVT ducted $2,200 + $400 + $500, net metering adder ~$7,125 over 25 years. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: Solar removal + reinstall for later roof replacement (mistiming penalty)
paybackNotes: Replace roof first if under 15 years remaining life. NREL studies cited: $3,000-5,000 bundling savings when roof + solar done together vs sequentially.

item: Vermont 8kW solar + battery, net after credits (facts.ts canonical range)
paybackNotes: From facts.ts 'vt-cost-solar-8kw' (verified 2026-04-15), the fact record backing the solar-battery-stack guide. [Federal 25C credit expired Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 rebate-stack guides — no longer counted as a rebate.]

item: Vermont Net Metering Group 2 (residential up to 15 kW)

rebate.amount: Full retail rate credit + $0.03/kWh adder for in-state solar

paybackNotes: Typical 8 kW system produces 9,000-11,000 kWh annually; adder alone adds $270-330/year in credits; ~$7,125 over 25 years on 9,500 kWh production. Installer files PUC paperwork.

item: Kitchen drawer organizers and pull-out storage
paybackNotes: Drawer organizers $30-80 (bamboo/wood); soft-close pull-out trash/recycling kit $80-150; floating open shelving $40-80 per wall.

item: Vermont window replacement, 12-window project (facts.ts canonical range)
paybackNotes: From facts.ts 'vt-cost-windows-replacement' (verified 2026-04-15): modern double-pane vinyl or fiberglass; historic district approval adds time but rarely cost.

item: Window replacement energy payback (single-pane to double-pane)
paybackNotes: Replacing a $1,200 single-pane double-hung saves roughly $30-80/year in heating cost; payback 15-40 years on energy alone. Comfort and resale value are the faster justification. EVT does not currently rebate window replacement on most residential projects.

item: Window replacement, standard double-pane vinyl/fiberglass, per window installed
paybackNotes: 8-window typical home: $8,000-16,000. Historic-restoration replacement: $2,000-4,000/window; historic farmhouse with restoration matching: $20,000-40,000+. Standard new-construction (2000s+): $6,000-12,000 for same window count.
